findings.reason: The protected Python solution finds the shortest distance between word1 and word2 in a single linear pass over wordsDict. When word1 == word2, it tracks the previous occurrence index and updates distance on each new match; when word1 != word2, it tracks the most recent index of each word. The solution runs in O(n) time and O(1) space; no candidate is required.

For distinct words, tracking the latest index of each word evaluates all candidate adjacent pairs; for identical words, tracking the previous match index evaluates every pair of consecutive occurrences without self-pairing.

A single linear pass over n words in wordsDict performs O(1) work per word, yielding O(n) total time. Auxiliary space is O(1) for scalar index trackers. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts wordsDict (List[str]), word1 (str), and word2 (str), returning the integer minimum distance between distinct occurrences of word1 and word2.

The approach accurately details single-pass latest-occurrence tracking, conditional logic for equal versus distinct target words, and O(n) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover occurrence-list memory trade-offs, all-pairs quadratic costs, equal target self-pairing prevention, and distinct target matching.
